@@ -0,0 +1,185 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+started_at="$(date +%s)"
+
+format_elapsed() {
+  local elapsed_seconds="$1"
+  local elapsed_hours=$((elapsed_seconds / 3600))
+  local elapsed_minutes=$(((elapsed_seconds % 3600) / 60))
+
+  if (( elapsed_hours > 0 )); then
+    printf '%dh %02dm' "$elapsed_hours" "$elapsed_minutes"
+  else
+    printf '%dm' "$elapsed_minutes"
+  fi
+}
+
+if [[ "${1:-}" == "--format-elapsed" ]]; then
+  format_elapsed "${2:?elapsed seconds are required}"
+  printf '\n'
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+vision_calls() {
+  jq -r '
+    def has_image($message):
+      any((($message.parts // [])[]?);
+        (.type == "file" and ((.mime // .mediaType // "") | startswith("image/"))) or
+        (.type == "tool" and any(((.state.attachments // [])[]?.mime?); ((. // "") | startswith("image/"))))
+      );
+    reduce .[] as $message ({ seen: false, calls: 0 };
+      if $message.info.role == "assistant" then
+        .calls += (if .seen then 1 else 0 end)
+        | .seen = (.seen or has_image($message))
+      else
+        .seen = (.seen or has_image($message))
+      end
+    ) | .calls
+  '
+}
+
+while :; do
+  payload="$(curl --fail --silent --show-error \
+    -H "x-opencode-directory: $PROJECT_DIR" \
+    "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_WEB_PORT/session/$SESSION_ID/message" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+  sessions_payload="$(curl --fail --silent --show-error \
+    -H "x-opencode-directory: $PROJECT_DIR" \
+    "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_WEB_PORT/session" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+  status_payload="$(curl --fail --silent --show-error \
+    -H "x-opencode-directory: $PROJECT_DIR" \
+    "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_WEB_PORT/session/status" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+  if jq -e 'type == "array"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$payload" && \
+    jq -e 'type == "array"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$sessions_payload" && \
+    jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$status_payload"; then
+    stats="$(jq -r '
+      def parts: [.[].parts[]?];
+      def tools: [parts[] | select(.type == "tool")];
+      [
+        (tools | length),
+        ([tools[] | select(.state.status == "running" or .state.status == "pending")] | length)
+      ] | @tsv
+    ' <<<"$payload")"
+    IFS=$'\t' read -r tool_count active_count <<<"$stats"
+    subagent_stats="$(jq -nr \
+      --arg root "$SESSION_ID" \
+      --argjson sessions "$sessions_payload" \
+      --argjson statuses "$status_payload" '
+      def descendants($all; $parent):
+        [$all[] | select(.parentID == $parent)] as $children
+        | ($children | map(.id)) as $ids
+        | if ($ids | length) == 0 then $ids
+          else $ids + ([$ids[] | descendants($all; .)] | add)
+          end;
+      ($sessions | descendants($sessions; $root)) as $subagents
+      | {
+          total: ($subagents | length),
+          failed: ([$statuses | to_entries[]
+            | select((.key as $id | ($subagents | index($id))) != null)
+            | select(.value.type == "error" or .value.type == "failed")
+          ] | length),
+          active: ([$statuses | to_entries[]
+            | select((.key as $id | ($subagents | index($id))) != null)
+            | select(.value.type != "idle" and .value.type != "error" and .value.type != "failed")
+          ] | length)
+        }
+      | [.active, .total, .failed] | @tsv
+    ')"
+    IFS=$'\t' read -r active_subagents total_subagents failed_subagents <<<"$subagent_stats"
+    token_count="$(jq -nr \
+      --arg root "$SESSION_ID" \
+      --argjson sessions "$sessions_payload" '
+      def descendants($all; $parent):
+        [$all[] | select(.parentID == $parent)] as $children
+        | ($children | map(.id)) as $ids
+        | if ($ids | length) == 0 then $ids
+          else $ids + ([$ids[] | descendants($all; .)] | add)
+          end;
+      ([$root] + ($sessions | descendants($sessions; $root))) as $tracked
+      | reduce $sessions[] as $session (0;
+          if ($tracked | index($session.id)) == null then .
+          else .
+            + ($session.tokens.input // 0)
+            + ($session.tokens.output // 0)
+            + ($session.tokens.reasoning // 0)
+            + ($session.tokens.cache.read // 0)
+            + ($session.tokens.cache.write // 0)
+          end
+        )
+    ')"
+    subagent_ids="$(jq -nr \
+      --arg root "$SESSION_ID" \
+      --argjson sessions "$sessions_payload" '
+      def descendants($all; $parent):
+        [$all[] | select(.parentID == $parent)] as $children
+        | ($children | map(.id)) as $ids
+        | if ($ids | length) == 0 then $ids
+          else $ids + ([$ids[] | descendants($all; .)] | add)
+          end;
+      ($sessions | descendants($sessions; $root))[]
+    ')"
+    vision_count="$(vision_calls <<<"$payload")"
+    while IFS= read -r subagent_id; do
+      [[ -n "$subagent_id" ]] || continue
+      subagent_payload="$(curl --fail --silent --show-error \
+        -H "x-opencode-directory: $PROJECT_DIR" \
+        "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_WEB_PORT/session/$subagent_id/message" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+      if jq -e 'type == "array"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$subagent_payload"; then
+        subagent_vision_count="$(vision_calls <<<"$subagent_payload")"
+        vision_count=$((vision_count + subagent_vision_count))
+      fi
+    done <<<"$subagent_ids"
+    changed_count="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
+    elapsed_seconds="$(( $(date +%s) - started_at ))"
+    elapsed="$(format_elapsed "$elapsed_seconds")"
+    speed_score="$(awk -v tokens="$token_count" -v elapsed="$elapsed_seconds" \
+      'BEGIN { if (elapsed > 0) printf "%.1f", tokens / elapsed; else print "0.0" }')"
+    access_links="$(< "${PROGRESS_COMMENT_TEMPLATE:-$(dirname "$0")/opencode-progress-comment-template.md}")"
+    ssh_section=""
+    if [[ "${AGENTSWEB_SSH_ENABLED:-false}" == "true" && "${AGENTSWEB_SSH_READY:-false}" == "true" ]]; then
+      ssh_section="🔐 **Temporary AgentsWeb SSH session is ready.**
+
+Run: ${RUN_URL}
+Host: ${SSH_HOST}:${SSH_PORT}
+
+Run this command while the job is active:
+
+Command:
+${SSH_COMMAND}
+"
+    fi
+    progress_stats="- Elapsed: ${elapsed}
+- Token count: ${token_count}
+- Speed score: ${speed_score} tokens/s
+- Tool calls: $tool_count
+- Active tool calls: $active_count
+- Active subagents: $active_subagents
+- Total subagents executed: $total_subagents
+- Total failed subagents: $failed_subagents
+- Image-context model calls: $vision_count
+- Changed workspace files: $changed_count"
+    validation_session_section=""
+    if [[ -s "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/validation-session-url" ]]; then
+      validation_session_section="🔎 **Validation OpenCode Web UI:** $(<"$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/validation-session-url")"
+    fi
+    access_note="This opens the currently running OpenCode session directly. Access remains available while OpenCode runs and for 5 hours afterwards."
+    access_links="${access_links//@SSH_SECTION@/$ssh_section}"
+    access_links="${access_links//@UPDATED@/$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC')}"
+    access_links="${access_links//@OPENCODE_WEB_URL@/$OPENCODE_WEB_URL}"
+    access_links="${access_links//@PROJECT_FILE_URL@/${PROJECT_FILE_URL:-unavailable}}"
+    access_links="${access_links//@VALIDATION_SESSION_SECTION@/$validation_session_section}"
+    access_links="${access_links//@PROGRESS_STATS@/$progress_stats}"
+    access_links="${access_links//@ACCESS_NOTE@/$access_note}"
+    body="${access_links}
+
+_Image-context model calls are inferred from image attachments in the session transcript. Message contents and tool details are hidden. Full logs are published in the completion release._"
+    if [[ "${PROGRESS_DRY_RUN:-false}" == "true" ]]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "$body" > "${PROGRESS_OUTPUT:?PROGRESS_OUTPUT is required in dry-run mode}"
+    else
+      gh api --method PATCH "repos/$REPOSITORY/issues/comments/$COMMENT_ID" \
+        -f body="$body" >/dev/null || true
+    fi
+  fi
+  [[ -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/response-comment.done" ]] && break
+  sleep 10
+done

+# CoD-Fidelity Browser Game — Live Progress Page
+
+## Research anchors (6+ high-signal, guiding implementation)
+1. Official MW4 hub — https://www.callofduty.com/modernwarfare4 — Purpose: visual language, campaign premise (Korea/NY/Paris/Mumbai), editions/progression framing.
+2. MW4 Multiplayer systems (NEXT) — https://www.callofduty.com/blog/2026/08/call-of-duty-modern-warfare-4-next-highlights-multiplayer-gameplay-systems — Purpose: Create-a-Class, Apex Attachments, Prestige paths, modes (TDM/Domination/Hardpoint/Kill Confirmed/Inflation/S&D/Gunfight/Kill Block/Combat Outpost).
+3. MW2 launch progression — https://www.callofduty.com/blog/2022/10/call-of-duty-modern-warfare-II-launch-progression-overview-ranks — Purpose: Military Ranks 1-55, Daily/Career challenges, Weapon Mastery camos, Kit Tiers.
+4. MW Beta Boot Camp HUD/controls — https://blog.activision.com/uk/en/call-of-duty/2019-09/Modern-Warfare-Beta-Boot-Camp-Gaining-Complete-Control — Purpose: canonical HUD elements (compass, faction/score/timer, crosshair, killstreaks, weapon detail), ADS/mount/mantle, colorblind/accessibility options. Guides our HUD layout.
+5. BO7 HUD guide — https://www.thegamer.com/call-of-duty-black-ops-7-cod-bo7-hud-themes-layouts-guide/ — Purpose: 9 HUD layouts, widget visibility, themes, readability/color customization. Guides settings + minimal/clutter tradeoff.
+6. CoD4 HUD reference — https://strategywiki.org/wiki/Call_of_Duty_4:_Modern_Warfare/HUD — Purpose: classic crosshair/inventory/stance/compass-star objective/ammo+grenade gauges/damage-direction arrows/red-veil + heartbeat regen model. Direct model for damage/recovery.
+7. BO7 Campaign Endgame intel — https://news.blizzard.com/en-gb/article/24243859/intel-campaign-endgame-in-black-ops-7 — Purpose: mission-oriented pacing, assignments, Combat Rating/skill tracks, exfil loop, unified XP across modes. Guides objectives + replayability.
+
+## Decisions
+- Original implementation + assets only: all art procedural on Canvas, all audio synthesized via WebAudio. No ripped CoD assets.
+- Tech: single-file `game/index.html` (no build step), Canvas 2D raycaster-lite arena (top-down/over-shoulder hybrid actually: 2.5D raycast corridor for FPS feel, fallback top-down minimap). Chosen for: immediate play, performance, touch support.
+- Fidelity targets mapped: compass+minimap, ADS + recoil/spread, 3 weapons, grenade/lethal+tactical, killstreak (UAV + airstrike), health-regen red veil + directional hitmarker, objectives star, killfeed, XP/rank persistence (localStorage), 3-mission campaign + endless mode, pause/restart/win/fail, subtitles, colorblind toggle, keyboard/mouse+touch.
+- Route split (judgeable pieces): (A) core loop+AI, (B) HUD/presentation, (C) audio/feedback+progression/persistence, (D) verification/critique.
+
+## Completed
+- [x] Research anchors recorded (2026-09-07)
+- [x] Core game built: `game/index.html` (46.6KB single file, JS syntax OK, HTTP serve 200 PASS)
+- [x] Independent critic pass (fresh-context general agent): 5 gaps ranked; largest = touch Mission-2 soft-lock
+- [x] Fixes applied + re-verified: touch USE/UAV/STRK buttons, auto intel pickup, pause on pointerlock-loss/blur/hidden, compass ★ objective bearing, ray cap 320 + step .08, kill ammo resupply, compass throttle
+
+## Evidence
+- Research: websearch results above, 7 anchors with URLs+purpose.
+- Gameplay: to be recorded after build (controls test, screenshots, console check).
+- Delivery: `game/index.html` single file, runs via any static server.
+
+## Blockers
+- None. Browser verification limited to code checks + headless DOM/logic test (no GPU screenshots in this env).
+
+## Current gaps
+- Need full build + self-critique loop.
+
+## Next exact action
+- Write `game/index.html`, then run syntax/smoke test, then critic pass, fix largest gap.

parts.text:
New active goal: ## Objective

Deliver a production-quality browser game centered on the Call of Duty experience for players who want a polished, immediately playable military-shooter loop. Use Call of Duty as the fidelity target: preserve its recognizable visual language, responsive combat interaction model, mission-oriented pacing, readable HUD, weapon handling, enemy encounters, progression, and replayable gameplay while creating an original implementation and assets. Ship the real web experience with responsive input and presentation rather than a static mockup or a flattened demo.

## Quality bar

- Research authoritative and representative Call of Duty references before coding. Search official materials, gameplay footage, screenshots, and interface views; select at least six high-signal anchors, record their URLs and purpose, and use them to guide the work.
- Inspect the actual running artifact with vision and direct browser interaction. Compare captures or blind A/B views against the selected anchors whenever practical.
- Deliver complete gameplay states and workflows: onboarding, active combat, objectives, enemies, weapons, damage and recovery, pause/restart, success/failure, responsive HUD, audio or clear feedback equivalents, and persistent progression where appropriate.
- Make the result polished, accessible, operable with supported keyboard/mouse and touch or controller-friendly alternatives, performant, and robust to error and recovery states.

## Execution

- Act as the orchestrator for continuous multi-day work. Own the complete outcome and keep delegating, integrating, implementing, verifying, and improving it; treat prototypes and demos as intermediate milestones.
- Have the lead choose the route and split the project into independently judgeable pieces.
- Give each important piece a separate builder and a fresh-context critic or verifier. Each verifier must inspect the actual artifact, compare it with the quality bar, identify the largest remaining gap, and send the work back for improvement.

Title: How The HUD Works In CoD: Black Ops 7

...
Black Ops 7 expands on one of the most popular new additions to the series, allowing you to fine-tune the HUD to your preference and even outright disable certain elements, like the minimap and compass. With this level of customisability, you can enjoy a more modern Call of Duty experience, or give the whole game a classic coat of paint.
...
In this guide, we'll be going over how you can

the HUD, making the game fit your playstyle, where to find some of the newer elements on offer in Black Ops 7
...
## How To Customise Your HUD 

To customise your HUD, simply navigate to the Gameplay HUD section of the Interface tab. From here, you can tweak a few core settings:
...
| HUD Bounds | Set the margin for HUD elements. |
| --- | --- |
| Scale | Adjust the size of the HUD. |
| HUD Widget Visibility | Toggle certain HUD elements, like the compass and minimap. |
| Vehicle HUD Prompts | Choose when the vehicle prompt fades. |
| Radar | Remove 2D map information to make enemy markers more visible. |
| Minimap Rotation | Rotate the minimap when you look around. |
| Compass | Displays your cardinal direction. |
...
## HUD Layouts 

Like with Black Ops 6, you can reorganise your HUD in Black Ops 7 from a list of pre-determined layouts. Each of these will adjust the placement of the minimap, compass, equipment, player icon, and more.

There are nine configurations to choose from as of writing, and each of these can be found under HUD Presets.
...
### Every HUD Layout 

| Layout | Style | Widget Positioning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard | Default layout, displaying each core element. | Minimap: top left. Compass: top centre. Equipment: bottom right. Player icon: bottom left. Radio: right side. Objective update: below the minimap. |
...
| Inverted | Flips the Standard layout. | Minimap: top right. Compass: top centre. Player icon: bottom right. Equipment: bottom left. Radio: left side. Objective update: below the minimap. |
...
| Classic | Black Ops 2-inspired HUD. | Minimap: top right. Compass: top centre. Player icon: bottom left. Equipment: bottom right. Radio: below the minimap. Objective update: left side. |
...
| Portrait | Core information presented vertically, designed for mobile video apps like TikTok and Instagram Reels. | Compass: top right. Player icon: bottom centre, slightly left. Equipment: bottom centre, slightly right. Radio: right side. Objective update: left side. |
...
| Drone | Centralised layout inspired by remote-controlled vehicle HUDs. | Minimap: top centre. Compass: bottom centre. Player icon: centre left. Equipment: centre right. Radio: right side. |
...
| Scout | Moves objective details to the bottom of the screen. | Minimap: bottom left. Compass: bottom centre. Player icon: next to the minimap. Equipment: bottom right. Radio: right side. Objective update: top left. |
...
| Target Tracker | Prioritises enemy tracking by consolidating navigation info to the lower centre. | Minimap: bottom centre. Compass: below minimap. Player icon: bottom left. Equipment: bottom right. Radio: right side. Objective update: top left. |
...
| Central Command | Reduces eye movement by positioning navigation and loadout details towards the centre. | Minimap: bottom centre. Compass: top centre. Player icon: right to the minimap. Radio: right side. Objective update: top left. |
...
| Frontline | All core information is lined along the bottom centre of the screen. | Minimap: bottom centre. Compass: below the minimap. Player icon: left of the minimap and compass. Equipment: right of the minimap and compass. Radio: right side. Objective update: top left. |
...
If none of these layouts are to your liking, you can customise them further by disabling core elements in the Interface tab. Simply open the Widget Visibility drop-down menu, and you'll be presented with a list of options:
...
- Loadout Information. 
- Minimap Visibility. 
- Compass. 
- Scorestreak Widget. 
- Mission Tracker. 
- Gobblegums. 
- Squad Widget. 
- Round Numbers. 
- Perks. 

Further down, from the HUD Info Visibility menu, you can also toggle:
...
- Player names. 
- Player & Streak Toasts. 
- Medals & Notifications. 
- Score Feed. 
- Elimination Feed. 
- Elimination ID. 
- In-Game Text Chat. 

In the Gameplay HUD tab, you can also toggle zombie healthbars and damage numbers.
...
## HUD Themes 

Black Ops 7 also introduces HUD themes, located next to layouts, which alter the UI's appearance. Right now, there are only two options available: Standard and Aetherium, which gives the game a Zombies makeover.

You can equip this in multiplayer, as well.
...
## How To Adjust Interface Colours 

Black Ops 7 also allows you to modify the colours of certain HUD elements, like player healthbars, via the Color Customization menu — found under Interface>Readability.
...
You can also design a custom filter, tweaking the colour intensity of the world and interface.
...
At the top of this menu is a list of palettes for different categories of colour blindness, including Protanopia, Deuteranopia, and Tritanopia, as well as the option to create a wholly custom profile, adjusting the colour of your teammates, party,
...
, etc., individually.

The green triangles represent your team mates and the direction of the pointy end of the triangle is the direction in which they're facing. The red circles represent your enemies, but only if you can see them or they're firing. If an enemy is behind a crate or another obstacle and is not firing or creating any noise, then it won't be shown on the compass. The star on the compass represents the direction of your objective. So if the objective is to blow up a tank, then the tank is in the direction of the star. If the objective is to secure a building, then the direction of the building you need to secure is shown by the star. 

### Ammo Gauge [edit | edit source]
...
On the bottom right is the ammo gauge. The lines show you how many bullets have been loaded into the gun, the numbers show you how much ammo you have left in total. When you press the reload key or run out of ammo, it will automatically reload. 

### Grenade Gauge [edit | edit source]
...
Slightly above the ammo gauge but still in the bottom right corner is the grenade gauge. It shows how many special and frag grenades you have. You can only carry 4 of each grenade at the same time, but the number gets renewed every time you complete a mission. Occasionally, you will find grenades on tables, when you go near them they will automatically be added to your total if you have less than 4. 

### Text [edit | edit source]
...
An example of text
...
In the top left corner there'll occasionally be messages like "Objective Completed" or "Game Saved". Once an objective has been completed you'll also see details of the new one in this area of the screen too. In the bottom left of the screen, only at the start of every mission, only there will be details of the mission (name/place/date). You may also see dialogue from your allies at the bottom of the screen. 

### Grenade Indicator [edit | edit source]
...
The grenade indicator

This will point to wherever a grenade has landed. If you see one of these then it means the grenade could potentially kill you. You can get move to get behind cover (you may still see the indicator), run away or get nearer to the grenade and throw it back. 

### Grenade Throwback Indicator [edit | edit source]
...
The grenade throwback indicator
...
If a grenade lands very near you, you have a chance to throw it back. This is normally better than running away as throwing it back if faster. You should immediately throw it back as you may not know how long the enemy cooked it for. They also do not seem to throw grenades back often. 

### Damage Indicator [edit | edit source]
...
An example of very bad damage

When hit, a red arrow shows the direction of the soldier who hit you. If you are hit repeatedly, your screen will turn red and you will be able to listen to your heart beating and heavy panting. If this happens, you are seriously hurt and need to take cover to replenish your health.

Today, it’s time to dig into Co-Op Campaign Endgame, the replayable Campaign Mode that’s much more than an epilogue; filled with challenges where JSOC continues their incursions into Avalon following the conclusion of the first 11 missions. 

###
...
After completing the first 11 Co-op Campaign missions, players will unlock Endgame, tasking JSOC with exploring the vast landscapes of Avalon, exploring The Guild’s remaining Command Centers while battling exposure zones leaking a mysterious toxin into the city.
...
Designed for 1–32 players in squads of up to four, Endgame offers near-endless replayability as players fight through escalating zones across this massive map, level up unique Skill Tracks and Combat Ratings, complete dynamic Assignments and escape to preserve hard-earned progress. All the while, continuing the main Player Progression and Weapon Leveling, as well as unlocking specific Camos for all 30 launch weapons.
...
In Endgame, every player works together during their deployment in Avalon. Squads can split off to pursue their own objectives or fight alongside others to improve the odds in tough fights, an especially useful tactic when approaching the area’s more dangerous zones, as shown above in the Avalon Tac-Map.
...
In short, you choose an Operator, customize your Loadout and then drop into Avalon using a wingsuit for navigation, exploring the vast landscape on foot or in vehicle, face down threats across Avalon, then ideally exfil after completion a variety of missions.
...
Your C-Link operating system unlocks full Loadout customization in the Endgame, giving each Operator the ability to choose their preferred tools for the fights ahead. Your ultimate goal is to gain enough power to reach the higher exposure zones, where something is leaking massive amounts of toxin into Avalon from there, and it’s waiting for you.
...
You begin by choosing one of the four available Operator Slots, selecting your Operator (from up to 24 of the available Operators). Each slot (shown in the top-right corner of the above menu image) represents a character on a unique power journey. Next, you choose a Loadout.
...
Endgame Loadouts (seen along the left of this menu) consist of a Main Weapon, a Melee Weapon, a Field Acquisition (a weapon you’ve found in a previous Endgame match and exfilled with), and a piece of Field Equipment. Explore further into Avalon to uncover Workbenches found across the province to upgrade your weapon’s rarity, which boosts its damage.
...
Once you select an Operator for your slot and customize your Loadout, you make perhaps the most important decision of all: Your Major and a Minor ability.
...
As detailed above, when creating a Loadout, players choose one Major and one Minor Ability for their Operator. The importance of these abilities cannot be understated: These grant new moves, allow the use of powerful weapons, also give unique tactical advantages, have a brief cooldown between charges, and define each Operator’s unique playstyle. As you progress through Endgame, it’s worth considering the Major and Minor Abilities available to you:
...
Gain power in a match by completing Objectives, uncovering intel and defeating enemies to raise your Operator’s Combat Rating and unlock Skills that amplify your combat effectiveness. Every time your Combat Rating levels up, your Operator is given the opportunity to choose one of two Skill Tracks or Skills. These Skills continue to expand as your Operator’s Combat Rating improves over time to the max level of 60.
...
### Co-Op Campaign and Endgame Progression
...
Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 unifies player progression across the entire experience for the first time in franchise history. Whether fighting through the Campaign, dropping foes in Multiplayer, or surviving in Zombies, every action contributes to global Player XP, including Endgame activities.
...
Players will earn XP, Weapon Levels, Weapon Camos, and Battle Pass progress while completing co-op missions and Endgame runs. The experience you build in the story connects seamlessly into every other mode.
...
Weapons level up across all four modes, with a dedicated Co-Op Campaign Camo Track offering 16 unique Military, Special, and Mastery Camos to unlock for the very first time. Daily and Weekly Challenges are also available in every mode including co-op, giving players fresh goals, XP payouts, and unlocks every day of the week.
...
Operators are dropped over the skies and must use their wingsuit to descend to ground level. Through use of the Tac Map and the C-Link overhead display, we spot various Assignments and Activities around the map. Choosing one that tasks us with stealing a vehicle from a convoy, we hop into an armored vehicle and chase after the target.
...
After some fierce engagements with enemy Enforcers, Deadeyes, Raiders, and other Guild mercenaries, we capture the vehicle and deliver it to the designated drop off. In turn, we’re awarded a Cache, letting us choose one of two offered grenade types, and our Combat Rating increases, opening the first Skill Tree. We’re offered a choice between the Surgeon and Berserker Skill Trees.
...
Because we’re more concerned staying alive for the long run, we pick the Surgeon Skill Tree to start off with. On subsequent Combat Rating level ups, we’ll begin unlocking Skill in the Surgeon Tree, keeping our Operator in top fighting form with faster healing, quick revives, and other benefits that help keep you and your squad in good shape. Though an Operator with a different style of play would choose from an entirely different Skill Tree.
...
Time is of the essence in Endgame matches. Before the match timer runs out, Operators must seek out a friendly VTOL exfil. Get to a pick-up zone, clear the landing area, and get out. A successful exfil lets you keep your current Loadout and Combat Rating. Make sure you get out every time, so you can push into harder locations and reap the greater rewards that await you.

# Harsh Critique — `game/index.html` (471 lines, read fully)

## 1. Top 5 Gaps (ranked)

### 1. CRITICAL: Touch build cannot finish Mission 2, missing streak/interact/sprint
**Evidence:**
* `86-92`: only `FIRE/ADS/RLD/FRAG/WPN/II` — no `E-interact`, no `U/T`, no sprint.
* `173-180,205-207`: `interact()` (intel pickup + manual exfil) only on `KeyE`. Intel requires `dist<1.2` + `interact()`.
* `196-199`: `stickR` only yaws `G.pa+=x*.09`; `sp=3.2` fixed `295`, no sprint modifier.
* `344`: passive auto-exfil exists, but **no** passive auto-pickup for intel — mobile soft-lock on `MISSIONS[1].intel=3` (`151-153`).
* `203-204`: `popUAV()/callStrike()` keyboard-only; no touch path despite `G.uav/strike` HUD `79`.

Violates “touch alternatives” + “objectives” directly.

### 2. HIGH: Desktop pause desync on pointer-lock loss / tab switch
**Evidence:**
* `183-185`: `pointerlockchange` only sets `locked` flag, never pauses.
* `179,282-283`: `togglePause()` on `P/Esc`, but browsers swallow `Esc` to exit lock without delivering `keydown`.
* Result: `locked=false` → `mousemove` dead, but `update(dt)` `286-287` keeps running, enemies `330-337` keep damaging. No `visibilitychange/blur` handler anywhere.
* `268`: `winMission` time `(now-G.started)/1000` includes paused time; pause doesn’t freeze clock.

Robustness + pause/restart fail under real use.

### 3. HIGH: Compass is decorative, no objective marker — CoD fidelity fail
**Evidence:**
* `30-33`: `#compasstrip/.deg/#objstar` defined, `#objstar` never used in JS/DOM.
* `426-435`: `drawCompass()` rebuilds `innerHTML` every frame, `width:44px` steps of `15°`, `left:calc(50%-scrollWidth/2)` — no smooth scroll, jumps, no exfil/enemy/star projection.
* `434`: comment admits it: `simple edge indicator via toast-free arrow` — unimplemented.
* Minimap `436-447` does show `★` + intel, so compass adds no value; CoD compass without objective bearing is a miss.

### 4. MEDIUM: HUD “responsive” + stance/weapon depth are fake
**Evidence:**
* `8,29`: `--hud-scale` never written; `fit()` `158-159` only resizes `canvas`, no HUD reflow.
* `66`: mobile response is `display:none` on `#feed` — kills killfeed/objective feedback on the devices that need it most.
* `79,160,294`: `#stance` hard-coded `STANDING`, `G.sprint/crouch` in state but never set except speed check `keys Shift`; no crouch key, no ADS spread UI beyond `425` scale.
* `200`: `switchWep` blocked while `reloadT>0` — un-CoD-like; no reserve pickup, endless (`339`) bricks to `dry()` loop when `mag=res=0` (`230-231`).
* `225`: `$('eqline').childNodes[0].textContent=...` fragile; breaks if whitespace/DOM minified.

### 5. MEDIUM: Enemies + render lack readability, performance unbounded
**Evidence:**
* `397-408`: `drawSoldier()` flat rects + circle, no walk/fire anim, death is `rotate(PI/2)` rect for `0.6s` (`250,317`); no directional facing, no muzzle flash on foes.
* `378-379`: occlusion `if(r.d<s.d-.4)continue` uses single center ray — edge sprites bleed through walls.
* `387-388,335`: tracers fake `moveTo(W/2,oy+40)->(ox+off,oy-20)`, foe tracer identical except flag unused.
* `229,355,357-364`: `cast()` `step=.05` to `24`, `num=W/3` — ~640 rays × ~480 steps ≈300k checks/frame at 1080p, no cap/LOD, `shakeX/Y` random per-ray causes wall shimmer.
* `168,316`: `randFree()>5` can spawn in LOS (pop-in); `diff=1+kills*.02` in endless scales enemy damage unbounded → eventual one-shot (`331,337`).

## 2. Quality-Bar Verdicts

**A. Complete states:**
* onboarding: **PASS** — `95-106` briefing, controls, settings, deploy/endless.
* active combat: **PASS** — `230-249,352-396`.
* objectives: **CONDITIONAL PASS** — desktop ok `261-267`; mobile M2 uncompletable (Gap 1).
* enemies: **PASS** (thin) — 3 types `147-153,169`.
* weapons: **CONDITIONAL PASS** — 3 guns with rpm/dmg/reload `147-150`; switch-lock + no resupply.
* damage/recovery: **PASS** — `257-260,289,345,395,464`.
* pause/restart: **FAIL** — exists `107,282-283,459,461` but desyncs (Gap 2).
* success/failure: **PASS** — `268-281,108`.
* responsive HUD: **FAIL** — `--hud-scale` dead, `feed:none` on mobile.
* audio/feedback: **PASS** — synth `137-140`, `mute/sub/flash` `129-135`.
* persistent progression: **PASS** — `118-126,226` rank/XP/DMR/best. No per-mission stats.

**B. Operable / performant / robust:**
* keyboard/mouse: **PASS** with Gap 2 caveat.
* touch: **FAIL** — Gap 1.
* performant: **MARGINAL** — works small, unbounded cost Gap 5.
* robust: **MARGINAL** — `116,452` frame/error catch + `localStorage` guards, but no lock/visibility recovery.

**C. CoD fidelity:**
* compass: **FAIL** — Gap 3.
* minimap: **PASS** — `436-447`.
* crosshair/hitmarkers: **PASS** — `81,47-50,255,425`.
* ammo/weapon detail: **PASS** — `79-80,409-424`.
* killstreaks: **PASS** — `203-204,252-253`.
* grenades: **PASS** — `202,310-312,347-350`.
* directional damage + regen: **PASS** — `260,289`.
* mission pacing: **MARGINAL PASS** — 3 missions + endless `151-153`; no in-mission scripting/checkpoints.
* rank/XP: **PASS** — `122-126,226`.

## 3. Single Largest Gap + Fix

**Largest: Gap 1 — touch cannot Interact/pop streaks → Mission 2 unwinnable on mobile.**

Concrete fix (no new engine needed):
1. Add `tbInt`, `tbUAV`, `tbStrike` buttons in `#touch` alongside `86-92`.
2. Wire with existing `hold()` helper `197-199`: `hold('tbInt',interact)`, `hold('tbUAV',popUAV)`, `hold('tbStrike',callStrike)`.
3. Safety net mirroring `344`: in `update()` after movement, auto-pickup `if(dist<1.2) interact()` or expand `344` to also collect `G.map.items` when touch (`isTouch`), so tap-target frustration doesn’t block pacing.
4. Add touch sprint: double-push `joyL.y<-0.9` → sprint speed, or dedicated `SPRT` toggle.

This one change flips two red bullets (touch + objectives on mobile) to green with ~15 lines, reusing `interact/popUAV/callStrike/drawMinimap` as-is.

--- .opencode-web/response-comment-tracker.sh	
+++ .opencode-web/response-comment-tracker.sh	
@@ -0,0 +1,185 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+started_at="$(date +%s)"
+
+format_elapsed() {
+  local elapsed_seconds="$1"
+  local elapsed_hours=$((elapsed_seconds / 3600))
+  local elapsed_minutes=$(((elapsed_seconds % 3600) / 60))
+
+  if (( elapsed_hours > 0 )); then
+    printf '%dh %02dm' "$elapsed_hours" "$elapsed_minutes"
+  else
+    printf '%dm' "$elapsed_minutes"
+  fi
+}
+
+if [[ "${1:-}" == "--format-elapsed" ]]; then
+  format_elapsed "${2:?elapsed seconds are required}"
+  printf '\n'
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+vision_calls() {
+  jq -r '
+    def has_image($message):
+      any((($message.parts // [])[]?);
+        (.type == "file" and ((.mime // .mediaType // "") | startswith("image/"))) or
+        (.type == "tool" and any(((.state.attachments // [])[]?.mime?); ((. // "") | startswith("image/"))))
+      );
+    reduce .[] as $message ({ seen: false, calls: 0 };
+      if $message.info.role == "assistant" then
+        .calls += (if .seen then 1 else 0 end)
+        | .seen = (.seen or has_image($message))
+      else
+        .seen = (.seen or has_image($message))
+      end
+    ) | .calls
+  '
+}
+
+while :; do
+  payload="$(curl --fail --silent --show-error \
+    -H "x-opencode-directory: $PROJECT_DIR" \
+    "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_WEB_PORT/session/$SESSION_ID/message" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+  sessions_payload="$(curl --fail --silent --show-error \
+    -H "x-opencode-directory: $PROJECT_DIR" \
+    "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_WEB_PORT/session" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+  status_payload="$(curl --fail --silent --show-error \
+    -H "x-opencode-directory: $PROJECT_DIR" \
+    "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_WEB_PORT/session/status" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+  if jq -e 'type == "array"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$payload" && \
+    jq -e 'type == "array"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$sessions_payload" && \
+    jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$status_payload"; then
+    stats="$(jq -r '
+      def parts: [.[].parts[]?];
+      def tools: [parts[] | select(.type == "tool")];
+      [
+        (tools | length),
+        ([tools[] | select(.state.status == "running" or .state.status == "pending")] | length)
+      ] | @tsv
+    ' <<<"$payload")"
+    IFS=$'\t' read -r tool_count active_count <<<"$stats"
+    subagent_stats="$(jq -nr \
+      --arg root "$SESSION_ID" \
+      --argjson sessions "$sessions_payload" \
+      --argjson statuses "$status_payload" '
+      def descendants($all; $parent):
+        [$all[] | select(.parentID == $parent)] as $children
+        | ($children | map(.id)) as $ids
+        | if ($ids | length) == 0 then $ids
+          else $ids + ([$ids[] | descendants($all; .)] | add)
+          end;
+      ($sessions | descendants($sessions; $root)) as $subagents
+      | {
+          total: ($subagents | length),
+          failed: ([$statuses | to_entries[]
+            | select((.key as $id | ($subagents | index($id))) != null)
+            | select(.value.type == "error" or .value.type == "failed")
+          ] | length),
+          active: ([$statuses | to_entries[]
+            | select((.key as $id | ($subagents | index($id))) != null)
+            | select(.value.type != "idle" and .value.type != "error" and .value.type != "failed")
+          ] | length)
+        }
+      | [.active, .total, .failed] | @tsv
+    ')"
+    IFS=$'\t' read -r active_subagents total_subagents failed_subagents <<<"$subagent_stats"
+    token_count="$(jq -nr \
+      --arg root "$SESSION_ID" \
+      --argjson sessions "$sessions_payload" '
+      def descendants($all; $parent):
+        [$all[] | select(.parentID == $parent)] as $children
+        | ($children | map(.id)) as $ids
+        | if ($ids | length) == 0 then $ids
+          else $ids + ([$ids[] | descendants($all; .)] | add)
+          end;
+      ([$root] + ($sessions | descendants($sessions; $root))) as $tracked
+      | reduce $sessions[] as $session (0;
+          if ($tracked | index($session.id)) == null then .
+          else .
+            + ($session.tokens.input // 0)
+            + ($session.tokens.output // 0)
+            + ($session.tokens.reasoning // 0)
+            + ($session.tokens.cache.read // 0)
+            + ($session.tokens.cache.write // 0)
+          end
+        )
+    ')"
+    subagent_ids="$(jq -nr \
+      --arg root "$SESSION_ID" \
+      --argjson sessions "$sessions_payload" '
+      def descendants($all; $parent):
+        [$all[] | select(.parentID == $parent)] as $children
+        | ($children | map(.id)) as $ids
+        | if ($ids | length) == 0 then $ids
+          else $ids + ([$ids[] | descendants($all; .)] | add)
+          end;
+      ($sessions | descendants($sessions; $root))[]
+    ')"
+    vision_count="$(vision_calls <<<"$payload")"
+    while IFS= read -r subagent_id; do
+      [[ -n "$subagent_id" ]] || continue
+      subagent_payload="$(curl --fail --silent --show-error \
+        -H "x-opencode-directory: $PROJECT_DIR" \
+        "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_WEB_PORT/session/$subagent_id/message" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+      if jq -e 'type == "array"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$subagent_payload"; then
+        subagent_vision_count="$(vision_calls <<<"$subagent_payload")"
+        vision_count=$((vision_count + subagent_vision_count))
+      fi
+    done <<<"$subagent_ids"
+    changed_count="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
+    elapsed_seconds="$(( $(date +%s) - started_at ))"
+    elapsed="$(format_elapsed "$elapsed_seconds")"
+    speed_score="$(awk -v tokens="$token_count" -v elapsed="$elapsed_seconds" \
+      'BEGIN { if (elapsed > 0) printf "%.1f", tokens / elapsed; else print "0.0" }')"
+    access_links="$(< "${PROGRESS_COMMENT_TEMPLATE:-$(dirname "$0")/opencode-progress-comment-template.md}")"
+    ssh_section=""
+    if [[ "${AGENTSWEB_SSH_ENABLED:-false}" == "true" && "${AGENTSWEB_SSH_READY:-false}" == "true" ]]; then
+      ssh_section="🔐 **Temporary AgentsWeb SSH session is ready.**
+
+Run: ${RUN_URL}
+Host: ${SSH_HOST}:${SSH_PORT}
+
+Run this command while the job is active:
+
+Command:
+${SSH_COMMAND}
+"
+    fi
+    progress_stats="- Elapsed: ${elapsed}
+- Token count: ${token_count}
+- Speed score: ${speed_score} tokens/s
+- Tool calls: $tool_count
+- Active tool calls: $active_count
+- Active subagents: $active_subagents
+- Total subagents executed: $total_subagents
+- Total failed subagents: $failed_subagents
+- Image-context model calls: $vision_count
+- Changed workspace files: $changed_count"
+    validation_session_section=""
+    if [[ -s "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/validation-session-url" ]]; then
+      validation_session_section="🔎 **Validation OpenCode Web UI:** $(<"$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/validation-session-url")"
+    fi
+    access_note="This opens the currently running OpenCode session directly. Access remains available while OpenCode runs and for 5 hours afterwards."
+    access_links="${access_links//@SSH_SECTION@/$ssh_section}"
+    access_links="${access_links//@UPDATED@/$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC')}"
+    access_links="${access_links//@OPENCODE_WEB_URL@/$OPENCODE_WEB_URL}"
+    access_links="${access_links//@PROJECT_FILE_URL@/${PROJECT_FILE_URL:-unavailable}}"
+    access_links="${access_links//@VALIDATION_SESSION_SECTION@/$validation_session_section}"
+    access_links="${access_links//@PROGRESS_STATS@/$progress_stats}"
+    access_links="${access_links//@ACCESS_NOTE@/$access_note}"
+    body="${access_links}
+
+_Image-context model calls are inferred from image attachments in the session transcript. Message contents and tool details are hidden. Full logs are published in the completion release._"
+    if [[ "${PROGRESS_DRY_RUN:-false}" == "true" ]]; then
+      printf '%s\n' "$body" > "${PROGRESS_OUTPUT:?PROGRESS_OUTPUT is required in dry-run mode}"
+    else
+      gh api --method PATCH "repos/$REPOSITORY/issues/comments/$COMMENT_ID" \
+        -f body="$body" >/dev/null || true
+    fi
+  fi
+  [[ -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/response-comment.done" ]] && break
+  sleep 10
+done

New active goal: ## Objective

Deliver a production-quality browser game centered on the Call of Duty experience for players who want a polished, immediately playable military-shooter loop. Use Call of Duty as the fidelity target: preserve its recognizable visual language, responsive combat interaction model, mission-oriented pacing, readable HUD, weapon handling, enemy encounters, progression, and replayable gameplay while creating an original implementation and assets. Ship the real web experience with responsive input and presentation rather than a static mockup or a flattened demo.

## Quality bar

- Research authoritative and representative Call of Duty references before coding. Search official materials, gameplay footage, screenshots, and interface views; select at least six high-signal anchors, record their URLs and purpose, and use them to guide the work.
- Inspect the actual running artifact with vision and direct browser interaction. Compare captures or blind A/B views against the selected anchors whenever practical.
- Deliver complete gameplay states and workflows: onboarding, active combat, objectives, enemies, weapons, damage and recovery, pause/restart, success/failure, responsive HUD, audio or clear feedback equivalents, and persistent progression where appropriate.
- Make the result polished, accessible, operable with supported keyboard/mouse and touch or controller-friendly alternatives, performant, and robust to error and recovery states.

## Execution

- Act as the orchestrator for continuous multi-day work. Own the complete outcome and keep delegating, integrating, implementing, verifying, and improving it; treat prototypes and demos as intermediate milestones.
- Have the lead choose the route and split the project into independently judgeable pieces.
- Give each important piece a separate builder and a fresh-context critic or verifier. Each verifier must inspect the actual artifact, compare it with the quality bar, identify the largest remaining gap, and send the work back for improvement.
- Work across as many sessions as necessary to reach the complete requested outcome.

## Verification

- Fix the largest remaining gap and repeat the build, inspect, critique, and improvement loop until the acceptance bar is met or an explicit blocker requires the user.
- Record concrete evidence for gameplay behavior, visual quality, responsive operation, recovery behavior, and delivery readiness.

## Progress

Maintain a resumable live progress page with research references, decisions, completed work, evidence, blockers, current gaps, and the next exact action so another agent can continue without losing context.

Start working toward this goal now.
When the goal is fully satisfied, summarize your evidence on a line starting with `[goal:evidence]`, then end your response with `[goal:complete]`. A `[goal:complete]` without a `[goal:evidence]` line is rejected and not recorded.
If you are truly blocked and need the user, state the concrete blocker on the line immediately before `[goal:blocked]`.
Use `/goal history` to inspect recent lifecycle events and checkpoints.

Limits: 10 auto-continues, 900s, 200,000 context tokens.

## How To Customise Your HUD 

To customise your HUD, simply navigate to the Gameplay HUD section of the Interface tab. From here, you can tweak a few core settings:

| HUD Bounds | Set the margin for HUD elements. |

### Crosshair [edit | edit source]
...
This is in the middle of the screen and it shows where you will shoot if you press the fire button. It will go red if you are aiming from the hip and move the crosshair over an enemy. If you are aiming down range, you will see the iron/Red Dot sight instead and it will not show when the crosshair is over an enemy. 

### Inventory [edit | edit source]
...
At the bottom left, there is your inventory, it shows you what you're carrying and what button to press to use it. On the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3, this will look different. 

### Stances [edit | edit source]
...
To the right of the inventory, it will show you what stance you are in. There are 4 that you can be in: standing, crouching, proning or carrying a partner. Normally you should either be crouching when you are stationary and sprint when you want to move. 

### Objective Indicator [edit | edit source]
...
On the bottom of the picture is the compass. As well as giving you directions you'll see green triangles and red circles. The green triangles represent your team mates and the direction of the pointy end of the triangle is the direction in which they're facing. The red circles represent your enemies, but only if you can see them or they're firing. If an enemy is behind a crate or another obstacle and is not firing or creating any noise, then it won't be shown on the compass. The star on the compass represents the direction of your objective. So if the objective is to blow up a tank, then the tank is in the direction of the star. If the objective is to secure a building, then the direction of the building you need to secure is shown by the star. 

### Ammo Gauge [edit | edit source]
...
On the bottom right is the ammo gauge. The lines show you how many bullets have been loaded into the gun, the numbers show you how much ammo you have left in total. When you press the reload key or run out of ammo, it will automatically reload. 

### Grenade Gauge [edit | edit source]
...
Slightly above the ammo gauge but still in the bottom right corner is the grenade gauge. It shows how many special and frag grenades you have. You can only carry 4 of each grenade at the same time, but the number gets renewed every time you complete a mission. Occasionally, you will find grenades on tables, when you go near them they will automatically be added to your total if you have less than 4. 

### Text [edit | edit source]
...
An example of text
...
In the top left corner there'll occasionally be messages like "Objective Completed" or "Game Saved". Once an objective has been completed you'll also see details of the new one in this area of the screen too. In the bottom left of the screen, only at the start of every mission, only there will be details of the mission (name/place/date). You may also see dialogue from your allies at the bottom of the screen. 

### Grenade Indicator [edit | edit source]
...
The grenade indicator

This will point to wherever a grenade has landed. If you see one of these then it means the grenade could potentially kill you. You can get move to get behind cover (you may still see the indicator), run away or get nearer to the grenade and throw it back. 

### Grenade Throwback Indicator [edit | edit source]
...
The grenade throwback indicator
...
If a grenade lands very near you, you have a chance to throw it back. This is normally better than running away as throwing it back if faster. You should immediately throw it back as you may not know how long the enemy cooked it for. They also do not seem to throw grenades back often. 

### Damage Indicator [edit | edit source]
...
An example of very bad damage

When hit, a red arrow shows the direction of the soldier who hit you. If you are hit repeatedly, your screen will turn red and you will be able to listen to your heart beating and heavy panting. If this happens, you are seriously hurt and need to take cover to replenish your health.

...
After completing the first 11 Co-op Campaign missions, players will unlock Endgame, tasking JSOC with exploring the vast landscapes of Avalon, exploring The Guild’s remaining Command Centers while battling exposure zones leaking a mysterious toxin into the city.
...
Designed for 1–32 players in squads of up to four, Endgame offers near-endless replayability as players fight through escalating zones across this massive map, level up unique Skill Tracks and Combat Ratings, complete dynamic Assignments and escape to preserve hard-earned progress. ...
In Endgame, every player works together during their deployment in Avalon. Squads can split off to pursue their own objectives or fight alongside others to improve the odds in tough fights, an especially useful tactic when approaching the area’s more dangerous zones, as shown above in the Avalon Tac-Map.
...
In short, you choose an Operator, customize your Loadout and then drop into Avalon using a wingsuit for navigation, exploring the vast landscape on foot or in vehicle, face down threats across Avalon, then ideally exfil after completion a variety of missions.
...

# Harsh Critique — `game/index.html` (471 lines, read fully)

## 1. Top 5 Gaps (ranked)

### 1. CRITICAL: Touch build cannot finish Mission 2, missing streak/interact/sprint
**Evidence:**
* `86-92`: only `FIRE/ADS/RLD/FRAG/WPN/II` — no `E-interact`, no `U/T`, no sprint.
* `173-180,205-207`: `interact()` (intel pickup + manual exfil) only on `KeyE`. Intel requires `dist<1.2` + `interact()`.
* `196-199`: `stickR` only yaws `G.pa+=x*.09`; `sp=3.2` fixed `295`, no sprint modifier.
* `344`: passive auto-exfil exists, but **no** passive auto-pickup for intel — mobile soft-lock on `MISSIONS[1].intel=3` (`151-153`).
* `203-204`: `popUAV()/callStrike()` keyboard-only; no touch path despite `G.uav/strike` HUD `79`.

Violates “touch alternatives” + “objectives” directly.

### 2. HIGH: Desktop pause desync on pointer-lock loss / tab switch
**Evidence:**
* `183-185`: `pointerlockchange` only sets `locked` flag, never pauses.
* `179,282-283`: `togglePause()` on `P/Esc`, but browsers swallow `Esc` to exit lock without delivering `keydown`.
* Result: `locked=false` → `mousemove` dead, but `update(dt)` `286-287` keeps running, enemies `330-337` keep damaging. No `visibilitychange/blur` handler anywhere.
* `268`: `winMission` time `(now-G.started)/1000` includes paused time; pause doesn’t freeze clock.

Robustness + pause/restart fail under real use.

### 3. HIGH: Compass is decorative, no objective marker — CoD fidelity fail
**Evidence:**
* `30-33`: `#compasstrip/.deg/#objstar` defined, `#objstar` never used in JS/DOM.
* `426-435`: `drawCompass()` rebuilds `innerHTML` every frame, `width:44px` steps of `15°`, `left:calc(50%-scrollWidth/2)` — no smooth scroll, jumps, no exfil/enemy/star projection.
* `434`: comment admits it: `simple edge indicator via toast-free arrow` — unimplemented.
* Minimap `436-447` does show `★` + intel, so compass adds no value; CoD compass without objective bearing is a miss.

### 4. MEDIUM: HUD “responsive” + stance/weapon depth are fake
**Evidence:**
* `8,29`: `--hud-scale` never written; `fit()` `158-159` only resizes `canvas`, no HUD reflow.
* `66`: mobile response is `display:none` on `#feed` — kills killfeed/objective feedback on the devices that need it most.
* `79,160,294`: `#stance` hard-coded `STANDING`, `G.sprint/crouch` in state but never set except speed check `keys Shift`; no crouch key, no ADS spread UI beyond `425` scale.
* `200`: `switchWep` blocked while `reloadT>0` — un-CoD-like; no reserve pickup, endless (`339`) bricks to `dry()` loop when `mag=res=0` (`230-231`).
* `225`: `$('eqline').childNodes[0].textContent=...` fragile; breaks if whitespace/DOM minified.

### 5. MEDIUM: Enemies + render lack readability, performance unbounded
**Evidence:**
* `397-408`: `drawSoldier()` flat rects + circle, no walk/fire anim, death is `rotate(PI/2)` rect for `0.6s` (`250,317`); no directional facing, no muzzle flash on foes.
* `378-379`: occlusion `if(r.d<s.d-.4)continue` uses single center ray — edge sprites bleed through walls.
* `387-388,335`: tracers fake `moveTo(W/2,oy+40)->(ox+off,oy-20)`, foe tracer identical except flag unused.
* `229,355,357-364`: `cast()` `step=.05` to `24`, `num=W/3` — ~640 rays × ~480 steps ≈300k checks/frame at 1080p, no cap/LOD, `shakeX/Y` random per-ray causes wall shimmer.
* `168,316`: `randFree()>5` can spawn in LOS (pop-in); `diff=1+kills*.02` in endless scales enemy damage unbounded → eventual one-shot (`331,337`).

## 2. Quality-Bar Verdicts

**A. Complete states:**
* onboarding: **PASS** — `95-106` briefing, controls, settings, deploy/endless.
* active combat: **PASS** — `230-249,352-396`.
* objectives: **CONDITIONAL PASS** — desktop ok `261-267`; mobile M2 uncompletable (Gap 1).
* enemies: **PASS** (thin) — 3 types `147-153,169`.
* weapons: **CONDITIONAL PASS** — 3 guns with rpm/dmg/reload `147-150`; switch-lock + no resupply.
* damage/recovery: **PASS** — `257-260,289,345,395,464`.
* pause/restart: **FAIL** — exists `107,282-283,459,461` but desyncs (Gap 2).
* success/failure: **PASS** — `268-281,108`.
* responsive HUD: **FAIL** — `--hud-scale` dead, `feed:none` on mobile.
* audio/feedback: **PASS** — synth `137-140`, `mute/sub/flash` `129-135`.
* persistent progression: **PASS** — `118-126,226` rank/XP/DMR/best. No per-mission stats.

**B. Operable / performant / robust:**
* keyboard/mouse: **PASS** with Gap 2 caveat.
* touch: **FAIL** — Gap 1.
* performant: **MARGINAL** — works small, unbounded cost Gap 5.
* robust: **MARGINAL** — `116,452` frame/error catch + `localStorage` guards, but no lock/visibility recovery.

**C. CoD fidelity:**
* compass: **FAIL** — Gap 3.
* minimap: **PASS** — `436-447`.
* crosshair/hitmarkers: **PASS** — `81,47-50,255,425`.
* ammo/weapon detail: **PASS** — `79-80,409-424`.
* killstreaks: **PASS** — `203-204,252-253`.
* grenades: **PASS** — `202,310-312,347-350`.
* directional damage + regen: **PASS** — `260,289`.
* mission pacing: **MARGINAL PASS** — 3 missions + endless `151-153`; no in-mission scripting/checkpoints.
* rank/XP: **PASS** — `122-126,226`.

## 3. Single Largest Gap + Fix

**Largest: Gap 1 — touch cannot Interact/pop streaks → Mission 2 unwinnable on mobile.**

Concrete fix (no new engine needed):
1. Add `tbInt`, `tbUAV`, `tbStrike` buttons in `#touch` alongside `86-92`.
2. Wire with existing `hold()` helper `197-199`: `hold('tbInt',interact)`, `hold('tbUAV',popUAV)`, `hold('tbStrike',callStrike)`.
3. Safety net mirroring `344`: in `update()` after movement, auto-pickup `if(dist<1.2) interact()` or expand `344` to also collect `G.map.items` when touch (`isTouch`), so tap-target frustration doesn’t block pacing.
4. Add touch sprint: double-push `joyL.y<-0.9` → sprint speed, or dedicated `SPRT` toggle.

This one change flips two red bullets (touch + objectives on mobile) to green with ~15 lines, reusing `interact/popUAV/callStrike/drawMinimap` as-is.
